files.file: new: workflow "tests", push/pull_request on main, one ubuntu-latest job, postgres:17 service, Python 3.12, pip install, pytest in backend

criteria.c: One new file only; parses as YAML with name/on/jobs. Nothing else modified (scratch PyYAML install went to the scratchpad dir, not the repo).
push and pull_request each with branches: [main]; no schedule or dispatch.
ubuntu-latest, actions/setup-python@v5, python-version "3.12", cache: pip with cache-dependency-path: requirements.txt.
postgres:17; POSTGRES_USER=ci_user, POSTGRES_PASSWORD=ci_throwaway_password, POSTGRES_DB=dailylog_test; ports 5432:5432; options --health-cmd pg_isready, interval 5s, timeout 5s, retries 10.
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://ci_user:ci_throwaway_password@localhost:5432/dailylog_test set on the test step; matches service env; DATABASE_URL not set anywhere.
Order: checkout@v4, setup-python@v5, pip install -r requirements.txt, test step with working-directory backend running python -m pytest -q tests.

PyYAML safe_load run (installed with pip --target into scratchpad, run with the scratchpad as cwd); parsed structure checked against criteria 1-6. Note: YAML 1.1 loads key "on" as boolean True, which is normal for Actions workflows.
NOT run: no local reproduction of the pytest run against Postgres, since it would need a clean venv and a temp Postgres on a non-8000 port. Not attempted.

tests.test: YAML parse and structure check: passes. Pytest suite: not run (7b).

commands_run.command: python -I -c yaml.safe_load(...) on the workflow, printed as JSON

design_decisions.decision: Used cache: pip with cache-dependency-path: requirements.txt (the optional caching, keyed off requirements.txt); rejected omitting it, since the spec allows it and it is low risk.
Health check 5s interval/5s timeout/10 retries; arbitrary but generous values.
Set TEST_DATABASE_URL at step level, not job level, to limit its scope.

implementation.self_critique: Real GitHub behavior is unverified. The local pytest reproduction (7b) was not run. If pinned requirements lack py3.12 Linux wheels, the install step would fail remotely.
